info.name: Bitnob Platform API
info.description:
# Bitnob Enterprise API

A high-performance Wallet-as-a-Service API for partners and developers:
non-custodial wallets, transactions, gas stations, on-chain subscriptions and
platform webhooks across multiple chains.

## Authentication

Authenticate every request with your secret API key in the **X-API-Key**
request header. Keys are scoped to one organization and carry a fixed set of
permissions; an endpoint returns **403** when the key lacks the required
permission. Treat the key as a credential — never expose it in a browser or
mobile client.

## Request tracing

Every response carries an **X-Request-Id** header. Log it, and quote it when
contacting support — it identifies the exact request in our systems.

## Rate limits

Every response carries the current rate-limit state:

- **X-RateLimit-Limit** — requests permitted in the current window.
- **X-RateLimit-Remaining** — requests still available in this window.
- **X-RateLimit-Reset** — Unix time (seconds) when the window resets.
- **X-RateLimit-Scope** — the scope the limit was applied at.

Read these proactively and slow down before you are throttled. When a limit is
exceeded the API responds **429** with a **Retry-After** header (seconds to
wait); retry only after that delay.

## Idempotency

Send an **Idempotency-Key** header (a unique value you generate, e.g. a UUID)
on **POST**, **PATCH** and **DELETE** requests so a network retry never
applies the same change twice.

- It is **required** on value-moving endpoints (creating transactions,
  creating addresses, refilling and sponsor-broadcasting gas stations,
  creating wallets); those return **400 idempotency_key_required** if absent.
- Keys are retained for **24 hours**.
- Retrying with the same key replays the original response byte-for-byte and
  adds an **Idempotent-Replayed: true** header.
- Reusing a key with a **different request body** is rejected with
  **409 idempotency_conflict** — generate a fresh key per distinct operation.
- Only successful (2xx) responses are stored, so a request that failed can be
  safely retried with the same key.
- An Idempotency-Key sent without authentication is rejected with **401**.

## Pagination

List endpoints are cursor-paginated. Parameters:

- **limit** — page size; bounded by the endpoint maximum.
- **starting_after** — return the page after this opaque cursor.
- **ending_before** — return the page before this opaque cursor.

Supplying both **starting_after** and **ending_before** is rejected with
**400 ambiguous_cursor**. Every list response is the same envelope:

    {
      "object": "list",
      "data": [ ... ],
      "has_more": true,
      "next_cursor": "b3JnOjE2ODk...",
      "url": "/wallets"
    }

When **has_more** is true, pass **next_cursor** as **starting_after** to fetch
the following page. Cursors are opaque — do not parse or construct them.

## Errors

Every error response is the same envelope:

    {
      "error": {
        "type": "invalid_request_error",
        "code": "invalid_cursor",
        "message": "starting_after is not a valid cursor",
        "param": "starting_after",
        "request_id": "req_01HX..."
      }
    }

**type** is the broad category; **code** is a stable, machine-readable
identifier — branch on **code**, show **message** to humans, and **param**
names the offending field when applicable.

### Error code catalogue

**invalid_request_error** (HTTP 400) — the request was malformed or failed
validation: invalid_request, invalid_json, invalid_body, empty_body,
trailing_data, type_mismatch, unknown_field, missing_required_field,
invalid_id, invalid_cursor, ambiguous_cursor, invalid_expand, invalid_chain,
invalid_vault_id, wallet_chain_unknown, invalid_transaction_data,
amount_precision_loss, gas_station_low_balance, body_too_large,
idempotency_key_required, idempotency_key_invalid, invalid_webhook_id,
method_not_allowed.

**authentication_error** (HTTP 401) — the request was not authenticated:
not_authenticated, auth_required, org_required.

**permission_error** (HTTP 403) — the request is authenticated but not
permitted: insufficient_permissions (the API key lacks the required
permission), ip_not_allowed (the request's source IP is not in the key's IP
allowlist).

**not_found_error** (HTTP 404) — the addressed resource does not exist:
not_found, route_not_found, asset_not_found, event_not_found,
gas_station_not_found, subscription_not_found, transaction_not_found,
vault_not_found, wallet_not_found, address_not_found, webhook_not_found.

**conflict_error** (HTTP 409) — the request conflicts with current state:
conflict, idempotency_conflict, wallet_archived.

**rate_limit_error** (HTTP 429) — too many requests: rate_limit_exceeded.

**api_error** (HTTP 500) — an unexpected server error: request_error,
internal_error.

**service_unavailable_error** (HTTP 503) — a dependency is unavailable;
retry after the Retry-After delay: service_unavailable.

## Webhook signature verification

The platform signs every webhook delivery with HMAC-SHA256 using the signing
secret issued when you create the webhook or subscription (and rotated via the
rotate-secret endpoints — the plaintext secret is shown only once).

The signature covers the canonical JSON object below, where **data**,
**event** and **timestamp** are the corresponding fields of the delivered
payload and **timestamp** is Unix seconds:

    {"data": <data>, "event": "<event>", "timestamp": <unix_seconds>}

The signed object contains ONLY those three keys — when verifying, build a
fresh object from the delivery's data, event and timestamp and exclude the
signature field (and any other body fields) from the HMAC input. Serialize the
keys in lexical order (data, event, timestamp), matching Go's encoding/json.
The signature value is:

    "sha256=" + hex( HMAC_SHA256(signing_secret, canonical_json) )

**Platform webhooks** (created via /webhooks) carry this value in the
**X-Webhook-Signature** response header. **On-chain subscription webhooks**
(created via /subscriptions) carry it as a **signature** field inside the
delivered JSON body — there is no signature header.

To verify a delivery: recompute the signature from your stored secret and
compare it to the received value with a constant-time comparison. Reject the
delivery on mismatch, and reject deliveries whose **timestamp** is older than
your tolerance window (a few minutes is typical) to defend against replay.

## Webhook event types

**Platform notification webhooks** (/webhooks) deliver these event types:
wallet.created, wallet.deleted, wallet.suspended, wallet_address.created,
transaction.created, transaction.signed, transaction.broadcasting,
transaction.confirmed, transaction.completed, transaction.received,
transaction.failed, transaction.cancelled, gas_station.low_balance,
gas_station.critical_balance, gas_station.auto_refilled, session.created,
api_key.created, api_key.deleted, policy.violation, kyt.deposit.held,
kyt.deposit.approved, kyt.deposit.rejected, kyt.deposit.blocked,
kyt.withdrawal.blocked, kyt.sanctions.match, kyt.alert.escalated,
kyt.screening.timeout, kyt.screening.requeued, kyt.screening.completed.

**On-chain subscription webhooks** (/subscriptions) deliver these event
types: incoming_native_tx, incoming_token_tx, incoming_nft_transfer,
incoming_internal_tx, outgoing_native_tx, outgoing_token_tx,
outgoing_nft_transfer, outgoing_internal_tx, tx_failed, tx_pending,
confirmation_threshold_met, confirmation_finalized, contract_deployed,
contract_executed, balance_changed.

## Versioning and deprecation

Pin the API version with the **API-Version** request header; omit it to take
the current default. Additive changes (new endpoints, new optional fields) are
not versioned and may appear at any time — write tolerant clients.

When an operation or version is scheduled for removal it is marked
**deprecated** in this specification, and its responses carry a
**Deprecation** header plus a **Sunset** header (RFC 8594) giving the date
after which it stops functioning. Monitor those headers and migrate before the
Sunset date.
